unit.title: An Email value object with correct equality

fund-csharp/13-equality-and-hashing/01-e.instructions:
**Skills:** IEquatable · GetHashCode  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Sign-up allows 'Ana@Example.com' and 'ana@example.com ' as two accounts. Introduce an Email type whose equality ignores case and surrounding spaces, and make sure it works as a dictionary key."

**Why it matters.** Normalised equality is exactly the case a record cannot generate for you. Equals, GetHashCode and the operators must agree, or hash-based collections misbehave.

**Your task.** Complete `sealed class Email : IEquatable<Email>` in the types section:
- the constructor trims the raw text and lower-cases it with the invariant culture; `Value` exposes the result; a blank input throws `ArgumentException`
- `Equals(Email?)`, `Equals(object?)`, `GetHashCode()`, `==` and `!=` all compare the normalised values; anything compared with null is not equal (and `null == null` is true)
- `ToString()` returns `Value`

**Worked example.** `new Email(" Ana@Example.com ") == new Email("ana@example.com")` is true, and a HashSet of both holds one entry.
hints: If every member works on the same normalised string, they cannot disagree with each other.
Normalise the text once when the object is built and make equality, hashing and printing all use that single stored value; let the operators deal with a missing value on either side before comparing.

Normalise the text once when the object is created, base equality, hashing and printing on that one normalised value, and make the operators treat two missing values as equal and one missing value as different.
